title: Customer-scoped Differential Eval Harness with Encrypted Reference Sets
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Problem: Model and config rollouts occasionally cause small but customer-visible regressions. Current global evals miss customer-specific failure modes because they mix diverse prompts and corpora. We need a per-customer differential evaluation system that detects regressions tied to config/model changes while preserving customer data isolation and compliance constraints.

Goal: Build a harness that runs differential comparisons between two model/config variants over a customer-scoped reference set (golden/reference prompts + expected outputs). Reference sets must be stored and used in a privacy-preserving fashion for Dedicated and Private customers. The harness should integrate with rollouts (canary/A-B) and surface per-customer delta metrics that can automatically block or flag rollouts.

Scope: MVP covers Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Hosted customers are out of scope for this ticket (future phase). The harness will support two modes: (1) Local Mode — runs entirely inside customer-controlled environment using encrypted reference sets and local evaluation agent, and (2) Aggregated Mode — for customers that consent to aggregated telemetry, compute deltas on a blinded, aggregated basis with strict sampling.

Non-goals: Creating new golden sets for customers (we will provide tooling to import), replacing general regression CI, or building a full federated learning stack.

Key constraints: we must not transmit raw customer prompts/responses to Redwood in Local Mode. Any server-side artifacts generated must be encrypted at rest and in transit. The implementation must fit into current rollout and alerting pipelines (Console + Optimize).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Per-customer eval harness can run on Dedicated and Private (local) deployments using encrypted reference sets with customer-managed keys.
2) Harness computes differential metrics (accuracy drift, toxicity delta, hallucination rate delta, latency P95 change) between baseline and candidate model/config.
3) Console shows per-customer delta dashboard and flags rollouts when thresholds are exceeded; alerts integrate with existing PagerDuty/webhooks.
4) No raw customer data leaves customer-controlled networks in Local Mode; artifacts uploaded to Redwood (if any) are encrypted and access-controlled.
5) E2E tests for Local Mode, including mock customer data and CI job that verifies blocking behavior for a contrived regression.
6) Security review completed and sign-off from Security & Compliance.
7) Performance overhead measured: evaluation agent should not increase average inference latency for production traffic by more than 5% when running in parallel sampling mode.
notes: 2025-11-12 - Created: scoped problem with customer-evals team after multiple post-rollout incidents reported by two enterprise customers; initial interview notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Customer+Scoped+Eval+Discovery

2025-11-18 - Architecture sync: decided on two-mode approach (Local Mode + Aggregated Mode) to balance privacy and product observability. Engineering prefers customer-managed KMS for Local Mode. Action: ENG to prototype encrypted reference set format (ENG-4123).

2025-11-24 - Security review kickoff: Security requested clarity on key management and threat model for reference set leakage. Decided to require customer-managed CMKs for on-prem and Dedicated, and use envelope encryption for any cloud storage. Security asks: provide proof-of-encryption and retention policy docs.

2025-11-30 - Trade-off decision: explored secure multi-party computation for Aggregated Mode but cost/time-to-ship made it a research spike. For MVP we will implement blinded aggregation + differential privacy accounting for aggregated telemetry, tracked under ENG-3987. Follow-up spike planned for MPC/HE research roadmap.

2025-12-01 - Design feedback from Console PM: dashboard must include per-metric baseline, candidate, delta, direction (regression/improvement), and confidence band. Also include a simple "block rollout" toggle per-customer with audit trail. Spec: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/customer-scoped-eval-design

2025-12-02 - Implementation notes: engineering proposes a lightweight local agent (Go) that: validates encrypted reference set, pulls candidate and baseline model endpoints (local), runs batched evals with sampling, uploads only encrypted, aggregated metric digests. Ticket split suggested: PM->feature spec, ENG->agent prototype (ENG-4123), ENG->console integration (ENG-4178).
